• Name: European freshwater crab (also Levantine freshwater crab)
  • Scientific name: Potamon potamios
  • Minimum tank size: 10 gallons (~40 litres)
  • Type: Semi-terrestrial
  • Breeding: Medium
  • Carapace size: up to 5–7 cm (2–3 inches)
  • Leg span: 10–15 cm (4–6 inches)
  • Humidity: 50–70%
  • Diet: Omnivore
  • Temperament: Aggressive
  • Lifespan: 6+ years
  • Colour: white-dark and purple-to-black pattern

Despite its wide distribution, Potamon potamios is listed on the IUCN Red List as near threatened because of pesticide pollution.

Potamon potamios is primarily distributed in freshwater habitats in Eastern Europe and the Near East. It occurs in the Balkans, Greece (mainland and south-eastern Aegean Islands), southern Russia, Cyprus, southern Turkey, Palestine, Syria, Lebanon, northern Iran, Israel (Dead Sea area) and Egypt (Sinai Peninsula).

Because of their wide distribution in remote areas, there has been limited mixing of the gene pool, which has allowed numerous subspecies to emerge. Currently 7 subspecies are considered valid:

  • Potamon potamios ssp. cyprion Pretzmann, 1962
  • Potamon potamios ssp. karamani Pretzmann, 1962
  • Potamon potamios ssp. karpathos Ghiavarini, 1934
  • Potamon potamios ssp. cretaion Ghiavarini, 1934
  • Potamon potamios ssp. palestinian Bott, 1967
  • Potamon potamios ssp. potamios (Olivier, 1804)
  • Potamon potamios ssp. schoenmanni Pretzmann, 1986 (Naxos Island)
Potamon potamios is usually found under stones in the shallow water of temperate rivers and streams. These crabs are adapted to be semi-terrestrial and can dig deep burrows into muddy substrates.

Potamon potamios does not require much space. A 10-gallon (40 litre) tank can house 1 adult crab. One male and 1 female can be kept together in a 15-gallon (60 litre) enclosure. Males should not be kept together because of aggression and territorial fighting.

Stocking is one of the most important factors when keeping crabs. Overcrowding is a major source of stress and in most cases leads to health problems, aggression and cannibalism.

They are excellent escape artists and easily climb vertical surfaces, so a tight-fitting lid is essential.

Potamon potamios is not a fully aquatic animal. It spends most of its life in water but still has some terrestrial activity.

Land vs water ratio: the water area should take at least 70–80% of the space in the tank.

  • These crabs molt (shed their old exoskeleton) in water.
  • In nature, water also provides more hiding places and is generally a safer place.

Water requirements:

  • They need freshwater only. Experiments showed that they could survive in seawater for at least 2 weeks, but they never voluntarily enter saltwater.
  • The water only needs to be a few inches deep, enough to completely submerge the crab and nothing more.
  • It should also have hiding places, since the crabs molt in the water.
  • Provide a variety of surfaces for them to get out of the water. Rocks or driftwood placed in the water can form small islands for the crab to climb onto.
In a classic paludarium setup, these crabs thrive in water with a pH of at least 7.0–8.0, KH 0–10 and GH 4–16.

Potamon potamios is an omnivore and an opportunistic species.

According to the study, it behaves as a generalist in its feeding habit, actively preying on frogs, fish and various small invertebrates, as well as scraping alga-covered surfaces or grazing on vegetable debris, mainly dead leaves and plants. Cannibalism also occurs between individuals of unequal size.

In paludariums, suggested foods include:

  • leaves
  • plants
  • vegetables
  • crushed snails
  • earthworms
  • dead fish or shrimp
  • frozen bloodworms
  • detritus worms
  • tubifex worms
  • blackworms
  • Diet type: Omnivorous
  • Food preference: mix of meat and vegetation
  • Feeding frequency: 3–4 times a week for adults, daily for juveniles

Feeding rules in captivity:

  • Leave food for 24 hours before removing it. To prevent water contamination, remove leftovers by siphoning before adding fresh food. Leaves can be left in the tank for several days.
  • Leave old exoskeletons. Do not remove molted exoskeletons; the crabs will eat them later.
  • Check their hiding places. They may drag and store food in hiding spots for later; check from time to time to prevent bacterial contamination.
  • Diversity. Crabs need varied food; change the diet periodically.

Potamon potamios is not social. On the contrary, it is known for aggressive and territorial behaviour, especially during the breeding season.

These crabs are active, both in water and on land. They are very agile and move between aquatic and terrestrial environments in search of food and shelter. Their semi-aquatic (amphibious) lifestyle lets them explore a variety of habitats. Males have been noticed to spread over surrounding land, straying up to 40 m (130 ft) from the stream at night.

They are primarily nocturnal, but also show some diurnal behaviour, especially large individuals.

The species can be classified as a secondary burrower. Although it can dig burrows in muddy substrates, it does not rely on them and does not spend all its time there.

  • Social: No
  • Active: Yes
  • Peaceful: No
  • Territorial: Yes
  • Burrowers: Yes

This is a medium-sized crab that usually grows to 5–7 cm (2–3 inches), but in exceptional cases can reach 10 cm (4 inches).

Distinguishing characteristics according to the study:

  • Carapace: slightly arched, smooth and concave. The anterior lateral margin is well developed with numerous very small, rounded teeth.
  • Gonopod: the first gonopod is conical or slender, without a swollen mesial part. Its terminal joint is elongated-conical, with the mesial part not curved outwards. The flexible area between the two segments is noticeably double-lobed.
  • Chelipeds: the claws are relatively large and unequal in length. They have high-ridged teeth that leave a gap when closed, set alternately with one larger and three to four smaller knots.

The taxonomy of Potamon is based predominantly on characters of the male reproductive organs (the gonopods).

Etymology: the genus name Potamon comes from the ancient Greek word meaning flood or rapid flow. The species name potamios comes from the Greek word meaning little or small stream. Overall, the name reflects small fast-flowing rivers and streams.

Lifespan: there are no studies on the maximum lifespan in the wild, where predation, disease and adverse conditions can shorten it. Under controlled, optimal conditions, Potamon potamios can live at least 5–6 years in paludariums.

Calcium: like other crustaceans, crabs depend on calcium, particularly during molting. It is necessary for developing and maintaining the hard exoskeleton. Insufficient calcium can lead to weakened shells and deformed limbs, so crabs need a balanced diet that includes calcium sources such as algae, or supplements formulated for crabs.

Plants: they are not plant safe. There is a very high chance they will eat, cut and shred any plant they can get, so keeping them in beautifully planted tanks is not recommended. Viable options are plastic plants, floating plants, or cheap plants you are ready to lose.
